title: What If
summary:
What If
Oil prices are "down" to the high $40's and everyone is breathing a sigh of relief. There are some important things we can think about: § new refineries in India and China have been built for medium to sweet crude; § there is limited spare oil export capacity for medium to sweet crudes; § spare oil export capacity is concentrated in sour crudes; and § refineries that process sour crudes are operating at maximum sustainable capacity. We might be at the crux of a supply demand crisis.

children.title: Europe
children.summary: Oil imports into Europe is net of production in the North Sea, Russia and the Caspian Sea region. In the past, oil imports fell as North Sea production rose.

children.title: Asia
children.summary: Domestic oil production in Asia is essentially flat with gains in China and elsewhere compensating for declines in Indonesia. Indonesia, an OPEC member, is about to become a net oil importer from falling production and rising consumption.

children.title: Vlcc Demand
children.summary: The model assigns flows of oil imports to various oil exporters in the Atlantic basin. Any deficit is satisfied by AG exports.

children.title: # Vlccs
children.summary: It is not the price of oil itself that matters, but the impact of oil prices on economic activity. High priced oil basically flattens out Vlcc demand whereas low priced oil encourages economic activity and, consequently, Vlcc demand.
